notes.title: Where are we?
notes.content:
As the game's development progresses it's harder to find time to write articles. But now it's time to update our future players.

As game development progresses, it becomes harder to find time to write articles. But now, it's time to update our future players.

First of all, I'd like to thank you for your support and for all the wishlists that have already been added. Then, I'd like to show you the new GSC logo:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45471854/da6c62f50f893cbe79ddc73f245c9fd4af0ca75e.png
Development Progress
For everyone waiting for the release of GSC, I can tell you that we are making great progress—especially considering that it's just the two of us working on all aspects of the game, from assets to coding.

Currently, we have completed the development of the game's main loop. This means that the player can already start the store, buy products, stock them on shelves, sell them, make a profit, and more. Players can also purchase store assets like shelves and console display booths. One of the mechanics we are particularly excited about is the exclusive and fun old-school credit card payment system, which we previously showcased in this post: Old School CC Machine.

For the DEMO release, GSC will feature around 15 different products, including two different consoles from the late '70s and '80s, about 10 games, and other items. It's important to note that the DEMO will not cover multiple console generations—although we plan to include them all as development progresses. I can confirm that by the Early Access release, we plan to have multiple generations and all the products available at that stage of development.

At the moment, we are finalizing some core features and fixing bugs to prepare for alpha testing next month. This phase will allow us to collect valuable early feedback. After that, we will release the DEMO and start preparing for Steam Next Fest and the Early Access launch.

Final Thoughts
We are super excited about the game's progress and would love to share more with you, but that's all we can disclose right now. Follow us here, visit our artwork and check our socials. Leave us a comment or a suggestion—at the end of the day, we are making GSC for you, and your participation is super important!

THANKS,
From Imponix Team (Daniel and Felipe)

notes.title: NPC Interactions in Game Store Chronicle
notes.content:
Bringing Your Game Store to Life: NPC Interactions in Game Store Chronicle

Our ultimate vision for NPC interactions is to create a dynamic and immersive game store experience. While not all features will be available at launch, we will continue expanding and refining these elements over time to bring your store to life in the most engaging way possible.

In Game Store Chronicle, your store isn't just a place to sell games—it's a living, breathing space filled with customers who browse, chat, and react to their surroundings. Here's a look at how NPC interactions will make your store feel more alive than ever.

Browsing and Finding Products
Customers don’t just randomly pick items—they scan the shelves, inspect products, and even react to pricing. Organizing your store strategically can influence their shopping experience. Well-placed bestsellers might fly off the shelves, while hidden gems might take longer to be noticed.

Conversations and Customer Reactions
NPCs aren’t just silent shoppers. They might chat about the latest releases, debate which console is the best, or even share nostalgia for classic games. Some may even give hints about what they’re looking for, giving you an edge in stocking the right inventory.

Checkout and Help Requests
Interactions don’t stop at the register. Customers will have different personalities—some are chatty, others are in a hurry, and a few might even try to haggle. Players will also assist shoppers who ask for recommendations, search for specific games, or inquire about trade-ins.

Your Store, Your Influence
How you organize your store affects NPC behavior. A cluttered store might frustrate customers, while a well-arranged layout can boost sales and create a smoother shopping experience. Keeping things fresh and accessible will be key to success.

Every customer in Game Store Chronicle has a story, and how you manage your store shapes their experience. Get ready to create the ultimate retro game shopping destination!

notes.title: What's GSC - Game Store Chronicle?
notes.content:
Game Store Chronicle: A Playable History, Not Just a Game

Game Store Chronicle isn’t just about managing a store—it’s about experiencing gaming history as it unfolds. Every console, game, and accessory you sell represents a milestone in the evolution of the industry, from the earliest days of home gaming to the breakthroughs that defined entire generations.

As time progresses, so does your store, with new gaming eras bringing fresh opportunities and challenges. Just like in the real world, anticipating trends and preparing for major releases will be key to success. Whether you grew up with these classics or are discovering them for the first time, Game Store Chronicle offers a one-of-a-kind journey through the history of video games, all from behind the counter of your very own store.

Let's get together and make this journey happen!
Follow us here to stay tuned on our posts and updates!
